newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debts recoup some spread losses.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debts recoup some spread losses.

text.p: Latin American Brady bond spreads narrowed slightly in late U.S. trade on Friday as U.S. Treasuries stood nearly unchanged after a short-lived rally, dealers said.
Traders quoted yield spreads to U.S. Traesuries as unchanged to five basis points tighter.
The bulk of Brady bonds traded hands in the opening hours following the release of a surprisingly sharp drop in the February Producer Price Index (PPI).
The 30-year U.S. long bond jumped over half a point in a knee-jerk reaction to the report only to quickly retreat to just above its opening levels.

Dealers welcomed the relatively calm market following confused and hectic trade on Thursday, sparked by a precipitous fall in the U.S. asset markets, where Latin Brady spreads widened by 20 basis points or more.
"For the first time all week, all we've seen has been buying. A lot of people are looking at Venezuela after Caldera spoke yesterday," said a dealer at a U.S. bank.

Venezeula's 81-year old President Rafael Caldera, dogged by peristent rumors that his health is failing, went for a short walk in the capital on Thursday to prove he is alive and well. On Wednesday, the markets were awashed with rumors that Caldera had died.
Venezuela Bradys were the top gainers on Friday. Venezuela PARs VZ675C20=RR gained 1/2 to a 72.50 bid and Venezuela FLIRBs VZ6C97=RR rose 5/8 to a 86-3/8 bid.
"Venezuela was the star performer amongst Latins with no good reason except some follow through from pretty good dealer and institutional buying yesterday," said a head trader at a U.S. bank.
Argentina bonds were also relatively active with Argentina Pars AR4C23=RR up 1/4 at a 64-3/4 bid and FRBs ARFLC05=RR up 1/8 at a 89-3/4 bid. Also, Brazil C BR8D14=RR rose 1/4 to a 76-3/4 bid.
Mexico bonds were quiet, with Mexico Pars MX625L19=RR flat at a 72-7/8 bid and Discounts MXFLL19=RR inched up 1/8 to a 88-5/8 bid.
Russia dollar Vnesh RUVNUSLNS=RR rose 3/8 to a 81-3/4 bid.

"Russia continues to be very strong. People believe the Russian deal (the restructuring of their old debt) still looks good to close by the end of April. Therefore, the deal risk spread trades that are going on and some net directional buying is still out there," the head trader said.
A Kremlin spokesman said President Boris Yeltsin is likely to announce a planned government resuffle next Monday or Tuesday and not on Friday as the market had widely anticipated.

In contrast, Bulgaria yield spreads to Treasuries widened between 10 and 20 basis points depending on the issue. Dealers said no news affected the debt and that the widening was driven by supply and demand imbalances. The Bulgaria FLRB fell 1-1/8 to a 45 bid by late Friday trade.
